results.longDescription: While tracking a band of Maquis rebels across the Badlands, the USS Voyager and her crew are pulled 70,000 light years across the galaxy into the Delta Quadrant. Stranded without a chance of rescue and with much of her crew dead, Captain Janeway joins forces with the Maquis and begins the long journey home. Determined to find friends and shortcuts wherever they can in this unexplored space, her crew must battle all-new alien dangers as well as shipboard conflicts — and keep their Starfleet ideals intact.

In season 4, Captain Janeway and her crew continue on their journey through space beginning with the conclusion of their encounter with the Borg in "Scorpion, Part 2".  Heroism is a major theme throughout the season and the crew demonstrates this quality best in "Nemesis" and "Scientific Method".  The dangerous nature of space travel is also highlighted in "Hunters" and "Prey".  Formidable opponents are found in "The Killing Game, Part One" and "The Killing Game, Part Two" featuring an alien race known as The Hirogen as well as in "Waking Moment's" featuring an alien race that 'attacks' during the human dream state.

In season 5, Captain Janeway and her crew face many challenges. The Maquis/Starfleet crew have many encounters with the Borg, including former Borg drone Seven of Nine's return to the Collective, who hope that her knowledge of humanity will help them assimilate Earth in "Dark Frontier." It is not only the Borg who pose as threats to the crew, but also an alien race called the Hazari, who ambush their ship in "Think Tank." Later, Paris and Torres get married, but it's not a happy occasion for long when the crew starts to disintegrate on the molecular level shortly after in "Course: Oblivion." Finally, the season closes when Voyager comes to the aid another Federation starship abducted by the Caretaker in "Equinox, Part 1."

Captain Janeway leads her Maquis/Starfleet crew through many interesting adventures in Season 2.  In "The '37's" her crew's loyalty is tested, and in "Tuvix" she makes a life-and-death decision.  Janeway's crew also encounters many challenges.  In "Dreadnought" B'Elanna must outsmart her own programming in order to save millions of innocent people, and in "Parturition" Neelix and Paris find themselves trapped together on a planet dubbed "Planet Hell" and become the unwilling parents of an infant alien.

High points for the Maquis/Starfleet crew in season three include "Basics, Pt. II," which resolves the cliffhanger from Season 2. Other top episodes from Season 3 include an episode featuring Q ("The Q and the Grey") and "Flashback" where Tuvok (Tim Russ) relives his time aboard the U.S.S. Excelsior under the command of Capt. Sulu (Star Trek alumnus George Takei). By the end of Season 3, the crew finds itself in Borg space only to encounter a species even more powerful and dangerous than the Borg.

The seventh and final season of Star Trek: Voyager begins where the previous season ended, with Janeway facing a deadly encounter with the Borg Queen as she is headed towards assimilation in "Unimatrix Zero, Part II." B'Elanna faces many personal challenges this season. Her relationship with Tom is put in jeopardy when he decides to enter a race in "Imperfection." In "Lineage," she is strangely disturbed by her unborn child's Klingon traits. In "Prophecy," a group of Klingons separated from the rest of their race believes B'Elanna's unborn child is the Savior foretold in their sacred scrolls. The Doctor also faces some difficult dilemmas, including being torn between his duty to Voyager and his conscience when warrior holograms rebel against their Hirogen creators in "Flesh & Blood" Parts 1 and 2. Finally, in the series finale "Endgame," Voyager's quest to return home is aided by a visitor from the future: Admiral Kathryn Janeway. However, Janeway decides to risk Voyager's shortcut home in order to destroy the Borg and save millions of lives.
